title: Preserve a valid guest observation when bridge requests remain pending
description: Host-session prerequisite of97341ad5. Own scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs and scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Today child close exit0 becomes SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION solely because session.pending.length>0, even after valid hello/observation/clean EOF; stop already aborts forwards and closes stdin. Make authenticated supervisor terminal observation+clean EOF+exit0 finalize once while cancelling/abandoning unresolved agent requests; never replay a request, dispatch queued work after terminal completion, or write late replies to closed stdin. Preserve real provider/protocol/timeout/abort failures and every malformed/duplicate/trailing-frame guard; cancellation cannot erase a prior failure or claim an upstream side effect was undone. Test pending active and queued forwards at successful finish, late resolve/reject/abort races, no extra forward/reply/onObservation, and negative no-observation/nonzero/partial/trailing-frame cases. Use existing stop/controller/timer ownership, no second session queue. Do not modify GUARD/pump or certification. Full external snapshot gate: node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs && (cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test). Depend on containment and provider-resolution task for explicit source serialization; parent follows this test file.
definitionOfDone: Valid hello/one observation/clean EOF/exit0 succeeds once despite unresolved agent requests; pending work is cancelled without late forwarding/writes.
Malformed framing, missing observation, nonzero exit, real timeout/abort and pre-existing failures remain failures in race-focused tests.
No leaked timers/listeners or repeated side effects; full runner+daemon regression passes in an external snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST, in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (DoD 1-3). Load test-driven-development. Use only the existing fakeProvider, openSession, exchange and until helpers and the HELLO/REQUEST/EXIT frames. Add no new harness.

1. Flip the one held H4 row that encodes the old contract. Locate it by its comment, 'An answer still owed when the job ends leaves the session unclean, so no observation is delivered': its forward never settles, then EXIT and exit(0). It now resolves {observation: EXIT, executionReady: false} and delivers onObservation exactly once. Nothing is written after the job frame (proc.written stays []), forwarded has length 1, and that forward's signal is aborted. Update the comment. No other H1-H8 row changes.

2. New test 'H9 a clean finish abandons pending requests: in-flight forwards are aborted, queued ones are never forwarded, and nothing is written late'. Each case asserts the result, run.observations, run.forwarded, proc.written and proc.kills, and that the caller signal's abort listeners are 0 after settle (getEventListeners).
- Active and queued: REQUEST id 1, whose forward never settles, plus id 2 queued behind it, then EXIT and exit(0). The run succeeds once; only id 1 was forwarded; nothing was written; its signal is aborted.
- Late settle after the finish: the forward resolves, or rejects, after `await run.promise`. After a further tick, still no write and no second onObservation.
- Abort-aware forward: it rejects as soon as its signal aborts. The session succeeds and no refusal frame is written.
- A forward still hanging past timeoutMs after the finish, while the provider exits 0 at once: success. Wait timeoutMs plus 50 ms and assert no kill and no late write, so no live timer acted.
- A forward that settles just before the EOF is answered once (written 1), then success: a reply is written at most once and never after the finish.
- A reply write in flight when the EOF lands (fake `write` callback delayed until after exit) does not fail the session.
3. Negatives in the same test, each with a request pending, each a failure with no observation delivered:
- EOF without an observation, or a trailing partial frame at EOF: SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION;
- exit(1): SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED;
- a frame after the observation: SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION;
- a forward timing out BEFORE the EOF (timeoutMs 100), then EXIT and exit(0): SESSION_TIMEOUT, because the prior failure is kept;
- a caller abort after the observation and EOF but before the provider exits: SESSION_ABORTED;
- a job-frame write that fails (fake `first`): still SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` and record the RED rows in the step note. At RED, the flipped H4 row and every H9 success case fail with SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The negatives pass at RED and must stay green.

The row: owe({timeoutMs: 1_000, fake: {hung: true}}), with a forward that never settles. It records begun = Date.now() after the forward is seen; the deadline started at or before that. Then sleep(500), EXIT and stdout.end(), and wait for stdin.destroyed (teardown). It sleeps to begun+1250, asserts kills is [], emits close(0) and runs succeeds(): one observation, nothing written, no late write, signal aborted, 0 listeners.
- Margins are 250 ms on each side. The deadline expires at or before begun+1000. Stop's kill timer expires at or after begun+1500, i.e. EOF plus 1 s.
- Node runs due timers in expiry order, with microtasks drained between them. So a late wake-up still runs the deadline's rejection chain first, then our continuation, whose close settles and clears the kill timer.
- QA's example was EOF at about 400 ms and close at about 1300 ms (300/100). I balanced it to 250/250.
- The H9 header comment now says 'only the expiring-deadline row races real timers, with 250 ms margins'. It used to say no row uses sleep ordering, which is no longer true.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of the task diff (efbb4101^ to now: guest-session.mjs +9/-4, unchanged this round; bridge test +144/-9). One real finding, fixed in this step.

FINDING (my step-1 draft of the new row could fail on correct code):
- Node keys timer lists by duration. processTimers runs EVERY due timer of one list (draining microtasks between them) before it moves to the next list.
- The forward's deadline and stop's kill timer share the session's 1 s list. My draft closed through sleep(begun+1250-now), a ~730 ms timer in another list.
- So a stall of 250 ms or more covering about 1.25-1.5 s ran the KILL before the close, and the row failed on correct code. The draft comment 'expiry order' was false.
- Proof:
  - A pure-Node model (/tmp/.../timer-order.mjs) with a 1.4 s busy-wait gives 'other' = deadline, micro, KILL, close.
  - A stall-injected scratch copy of the draft fails on correct code with SESSION_TIMEOUT (case C).

FIX (test only):
- `const closeDue = sleep(1_000)` is created right after owe() returns, which is after the forward's deadline joined the 1 s list. The EOF (and the kill timer) comes 500 ms later.
- List order is therefore deadline, close, kill. The close's settle clears the kill timer (clearTimeout nulls _onTimeout, so listOnTimeout skips it), however late the loop wakes.
- The row comment and the H9 header were rewritten to say this.
- Evidence:
  - The model's 'same' run gives deadline, micro, close, with no KILL.
  - Stall-injected scratch copies: A (new row, correct code) PASS; B (new row, M03) FAIL SESSION_TIMEOUT; C (draft, correct) FAIL; D (draft, no stall) PASS.
  - QA's 19-mutant sweep on the final bytes (sha256 96761ed7c289...): control passes, M01-M16 and M18 killed (M03 included), M17 equivalent.
  - 24/24 concurrent H9 runs pass.
  - Fresh checkRefs gate on the final bytes, HEAD 7031d6bd (my files are unchanged from efbb4101; that commit only touched .moe/tasks): daemon 215 files, 6341 passed, 20 skipped; runner 636 tests, 633 pass, 0 fail, 3 env skips; GATE_EXIT=0.

Plan checklist (runtime unchanged, rechecked):
- No forward or write after closing: loop head, post-reply check, reply's null after the probe; the job frame is the first write.
- onObservation runs once, never after a failure (M14).
- `??=` only (M08).
- settle clears timers (M09, plus the new row's kill-timer clear).
- An abort-ignoring forward can't block settle ('past', 'expiring').
- A hung provider still gives SESSION_TIMEOUT with SIGKILL (H4).
- receive(), MAX_PENDING and the replay guards are untouched.

THEORETICAL residual: a full stall of about 1 s or more between the forward call and owe()'s 10 ms poll returning lets the deadline fire before the EOF. That is legitimately a session timeout, the same risk class as every timer row.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Waiting for pending forwards to settle before resolving: rejected. A forward can hang until timeoutMs, and the guest has already ended the job. The task asks to abandon them, not to drain them. 2) Reporting an abandoned-request count in the result: rejected, because it changes the {observation, executionReady} shape that runAgentJob and the H rows consume, and the DoD asks for no new field. 3) Ignoring every failure after the clean EOF: rejected. A job-frame write failure, a caller abort, a nonzero or killed provider and stop's kill-timer timeout are real and stay failures. Only pump's own teardown artifacts are dropped.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- At the clean EOF, the stdout 'end' handler calls stop(session) with no code: it sets closing, aborts the controller and destroys stdin. The child 'close' handler then decides.
- pump keeps pending[0] until its reply is written, so an aborted forward leaves pending non-empty. That is the sole cause of today's SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (the governor's 97341ad5 note cites guest-session.mjs:169).
- The held H4 'unanswered' row asserts the old contract and must be flipped. The AJ5 hello-only row in local-runner.test.mjs (no observation) stays a violation.
- Deps: a4a729dd touches guest-supervisor.py plus a new local-runner-guard.test.mjs, and 92307adc does not touch guest-session.mjs or this test file. Both edges order work, they don't share files. The parent 97341ad5 follows this row on local-runner-bridge.test.mjs.
planningNotes.risks:
- Timing-sensitive tests: drive every race with explicit promise control and until() checks, never sleep-based ordering except the single timeoutMs+50 ms no-live-timer check.
- The snapshot gate runs npm ci and a build in a temp dir (network, a few minutes). Never in the shared checkout.
